Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi Evan / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday 1 quick recap and the follow-ups I promised:

Summary of what I heard
- Primary goal: move our conversational summarization + retrieval assistant from Hosted API to Dedicated capacity for predictable latency and lower unit cost.
- Target workload: primarily 70B-class open models (Llama-2 family discussed).
- Current pilot: ~5k daily active users on Hosted API with spikes during campaigns.

Sizing info we need to finalize next steps
- TPS / concurrency targets: steady TPS and peak burst TPS you expect.
- Token mix: avg prompt tokens, avg generated tokens, percent of long-context (2k+ tokens).
- Latency SLO: p95 target for generation in ms.
- GPU preference: any constraints (H100 vs A100 vs L4).
- Security/network: Dedicated in our managed cloud vs Private VPC/on-prem.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Please confirm steady and peak TPS and token mix; share your capacity snapshot if available.
2) I will loop in our infra lead (Aditya) to draft an initial GPU count + autoscale plan.
3) Proposed 30-min sizing call next week; I have Tue/Wed afternoons PT open.

I attached a simple capacity-snapshot.xlsx template and our 70B inference profile for reference; will upload after your reply.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Evan Brooks <evan@streamly.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Thanks Marissa 1 great summary. Numbers from our end (estimate):

Workload / model
- 70B open model for chat + summarization, interactive latency-sensitive.

Traffic profile (estimate)
- Baseline TPS: ~20 req/s.
- Peak burst TPS: up to ~150 req/s during short promotional windows (5-10 minutes).
- Concurrency: platform-level concurrency is what matters; typical user 1-2 concurrent requests.

Token mix
- Avg prompt tokens: ~600.
- Avg generated tokens: ~150.
- ~25-30% of requests include long-context >2k tokens.

Latency / SLO
- Target p95: <= 350 ms for ~150-token responses; higher acceptable for long-context cases.

GPU preference
- Prefer H100s for performance; open to A100 80GB if costs materially better.

Deployment
- Dedicated managed environment is fine initially; Private VPC later if needed for compliance.

I attached our pilot export (capacity-snapshot.xlsx). Available for sizing call Tue 2026-03-31 2:00pm PT or Wed 2026-04-01 afternoon PT.

--Evan

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@streamly.com>, Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@streamly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-31T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up 1 initial sizing recommendation

Hi Evan / Alex 1 nice to meet you. Based on the profile (70B model, 600/150 token mix, baseline 20 TPS, bursts to 150 TPS, p95 <= 350ms), here is an initial conservative sizing to discuss on the call:

Recommendation summary
- GPU type: H100 80GB preferred for low-latency 70B in fp16. A100 80GB is possible with quantization but expect higher p95.

Baseline config (20 TPS)
- 3 x H100 (primary pool) with continuous batching and prefix/KV caching 1 should cover baseline with headroom.

Burst/autoscale (to 150 TPS)
- Autoscale up to ~8-10 GPUs for short promotional spikes; exact count depends on batching and long-context hit rate.

Long-context handling
- Long-context (2k+ tokens) increases memory + latency; consider routing them to reserved GPUs. If 25-30% long, plan 1-2 reserved H100s or extra autoscale headroom.

Quantization tradeoffs
- q4_0/q4_k can reduce memory footprint ~30-40% and lower costs; we'd run evals to validate output quality.

Estimated cost band
- Baseline (3x H100) monthly cost: conservative mid-range estimate; we will refine with commitment/term.

Next steps
- I will review your capacity-snapshot and produce a machine-by-machine estimate before our call.
- Prepare a short sizing worksheet to share in the invite.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
